requirements.statement: Every counted verification run of a feature is recorded in .trd-state/<feature>/implement.json as functional_verification.runs (one entry per run). The count carries across /implement-trd's verification pass, /verify-build, /refine-verification and every --resume of either. No command starts a fresh count, and resuming an interrupted run does not add a second entry.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O1 (source: investigation Objectives O1). Must pass: yes.

requirements.statement: When a feature already has as many counted runs as the limit allows, /verify-build (and /implement-trd's own verification pass) starts no further run. It dispatches nothing, writes one ruling request listing everything still open, and ends on that request.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O2. Must pass: yes.

requirements.statement: When a feature has reached the limit, /refine-verification writes no verification-plan.md. It writes (or re-reads) the same ruling request and ends on it.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O3. Must pass: yes.

requirements.statement: A run that ends not satisfied and brings the count to the limit names the ruling request as its NEXT step, not /refine-verification.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O4. Must pass: no.

requirements.statement: The ruling request lists every criterion still open, in plain words, with its cause and how many runs it stayed open. It offers exactly three outcomes (ship as is, fix one named thing, drop it), each with the step that carries it out. It is addressed to the product PM, who may escalate to the owner.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O5. Must pass: no.

requirements.statement: The limit is a setting, ensemble.verificationRunLimit in .claude/settings.json, defaulting to 2 when absent. A refresh never overwrites an owner's value.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O6. Must pass: no.

requirements.statement: Shipping or dropping an open criterion through the ruling leaves it filed as a defect issue in the project's tracker, as every other waived criterion is. (The TRD says the library proves the waiver rows exist and listWaived returns them; the filing itself is outside what this environment can prove.)
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O7 (standing owner rule, 2026-11-12). Must pass: yes.

requirements.statement: The vendored runtime under .claude/ and the packages/full distribution carry exactly the edited packages/core files, with identical content. A new library is symlinked into packages/full/lib/.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O8 (constitution.md Architecture Invariants, Vendored Runtime).

requirements.statement: Tests pass, with unit coverage at or above 60% and integration coverage at or above 50% where integration tests apply.
requirements.source: TRD section 1.1 Objectives, O9 (constitution.md Quality Gates). No task row lists O9 in its Serves column; each B and D task carries its own tests.

New prose test file. Dependencies: VRL-B001, VRL-B002.

Reference and history: docs/reference/verification.md, implement-trd.md and other-commands.md describe the limit, setting, counting rules and ruling request; AMENDED marker on docs/TRD/refine-verification.md O4 row only; CHANGELOG Unreleased entry. Dependencies: VRL-D001, VRL-D002, VRL-D003.

Evidence under .trd-state/cap-verification-runs-per-feature/evidence/live/VRL-T001/. Deferred by design (needs headless model sessions; set aside by /implement-trd unless --include-deferred). Dependencies: VRL-B003, VRL-D002, VRL-D003.
touches: No tracked source file. Writes only under .trd-state/cap-verification-runs-per-feature/evidence/live/VRL-T001/** and the throwaway slot .trd-state/cap-verification-runs-per-feature/evidence/live/work/slot-1, plus lines appended to .trd-state/cap-verification-runs-per-feature/evidence/live-manifest.jsonl (gitignored).

open_questions: Source PRD: no docs/PRD file exists for this feature. The TRD header's Source PRD is docs/plan/cap-verification-runs-per-feature.investigation.md, so its Objectives table was used as the PRD. That file's own Open Questions section reads 'none'.

TRD Open Questions, OQ-1 (should runs made before this ships count toward a limit?): assumed no backfill; runs starts empty, so an in-flight feature gets two more runs. Why it matters: a feature already on its third cycle is not stopped. If wrong: a backfill from report history is needed, and none is kept, so it would be a guess.

TRD Open Questions, OQ-2 (does a setup-failure run count?): assumed yes, since it is a dispatch of the workflow (D4), and at the limit it makes a ruling due (D13). Why it matters: a broken environment can spend the PM's budget without checking code. If wrong: exclude setup-failure in start/finish (one-line rule in VRL-B001).

TRD Open Questions, OQ-3 (after a 'fix one named thing' ruling, what proves the fix?): assumed /amend's own check battery, then /audit-build, with no further functional-verification run (D9). Why it matters: the fixed criterion stays open in verification-state.json. If wrong: grant one uncounted single-criterion re-proof, which changes D4 and /verify-build's --criteria section.

TRD Open Questions, OQ-4 (does 'drop it' mean the open criteria or the whole feature?): assumed the open criteria, each waived 'dropped by ruling' and filed, then /audit-build. Why it matters: a PM who meant abandon gets a closed feature with filed issues. If wrong: add a feature-abandon step to the drop outcome text.

TRD Open Questions, OQ-5 (does --reset-state clear the count?): assumed yes, since it deletes implement.json after the owner types 'confirm', and D5's merge cannot see a deleted file. This is the one owner-confirmed exception to O1. If wrong: --reset-state must carry runs into the fresh file.
TRD Open Questions, OQ-6 (what may the limit be set to?): assumed any integer of at least 1, with no 'off' value. If wrong: add null or 'none' as no limit in readLimit.

TRD Open Questions, OQ-7 (recordNonBlockingFollowups stamps foundBy 'verify-functional' on every row; acceptable for ruling rows?): assumed yes, since the summary carries the ruling reason and the gate reads only the '[non-blocking] ' prefix. If wrong: add an optional foundBy parameter in VRL-B001.
could_not_verify: TRD 'Could Not Verify' section (verbatim intent): nothing in the TRD is left unverified after the 2026-11-16 /audit-trd run. It lists four claims as confirmed, not open: (a) definition problems are stored as status 'not_met' with settled 'definition-problem' (packages/core/workflows/verify-functional.js); (b) docs/reference/verification.md, implement-trd.md and other-commands.md each mention the loop's caps and /refine-verification; (c) /verify-build persists functional_verification.environments and .fix by the set-in-memory-then-save pattern of section 3.6a, so the stale-save risk (TR1) applies to the fix loop; (d) no test pins the absence of a functional_verification.runs key; the only pin on the eleven-kind count is packages/core/lib/artifacts.test.js:28-30 plus two comments in artifacts.js.

TRD 'Verification Environment' limits (stated in the TRD, not in the Could Not Verify section): claude --remote sessions and failures that occur only on the GitHub Actions runner are not checkable here. So is a real defect issue filed in a tracker by waived-defects.js gate after a ship or drop ruling; VRL-B001 proves the rows exist and listWaived returns them, not the filing.
Investigation document's own sections: it has Objectives, Intended Change, Decision, Grounding and Open Questions only. It has no Could Not Verify section, so none was captured from it.

Task-level acceptance criteria (the long 'Acceptance Criteria' cells in TRD section 4, lines ~233-250) were not copied into this map. They are checkable promises, so verifiers must read them at those lines. The D1-D14 decisions in TRD section 1.2 also carry checkable statements (for example D12's exit-non-zero rule and D5's merge rule) that appear only in the task rows, not as separate requirements here.
